newsitem.title: CHINA: Britain, China sign deal for China London listing.
newsitem.headline: Britain, China sign deal for China London listing.

text.p: Britain and China on Monday signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) in Beijing to allow capital-hungry mainland companies to list on the London Stock Exchange, British officials said.

The agreement was signed in Beijing's Great Hall of the People by British officials and representatives of China's State Council, or cabinet, and the China Securities Regulatory Commission, the British Embassy said in a statement.

"The signing of the Sino-British MOU on Regulation of Securities and Futures will provide a channel for cooperation among China and U.K. securities and futures regulators (and) lay a foundation for Chinese enterprises raising funds in the UK," the statement said.

It gave no details of when the first Chinese companies were expected to list on the London exchange. Analysts say many Chinese firms are eager to use a London listing to tap into Europe's huge capital resources.
Some Chinese companies are listed in Hong Kong, while a handful are traded in New York. China has already signed a similar memorandum of understanding with Singapore.
